quests.question: If you freeze water,
options: it would have turned into ice.
quests.correctAnswer: it would have turned into ice.
quests.hint: Freezing water always produces ice - zero conditional for a physical fact.
quests.explanation: Zero conditional = scientific facts. Water ALWAYS freezes into ice - no exceptions. Both clauses: present simple. 'Will turn' is a future prediction (1st conditional); 'would turn' is hypothetical (2nd conditional). Laws of physics = zero conditional.

quests.question: If they study together every evening,
quests.hint: Studying together is a real, achievable habit - first conditional with 'will'.
quests.explanation: First conditional = real, achievable futures. Studying together is genuinely possible. If they do it (present simple), they will improve (will + infinitive - the real benefit). 'Would improve' makes it imaginary - as if studying together is just a fantasy.

quests.question: If he had more free time,
options: he would have taken up painting.
quests.hint: He lacks free time - second conditional imagines an unreal present situation.
quests.explanation: Second conditional = imaginary present. He doesn't have much free time (past simple 'had' = imaginary). If he did (imaginary), he would take up painting (would + infinitive). 'Would have taken up' is 3rd conditional - past imaginary.

quests.question: If he had listened to the advice,

quests.explanation: Third conditional = unreal past. He didn't listen to the advice (past perfect = what he failed to do). If he had (imaginary), he would have avoided the problem (would have + past participle - the missed outcome).

quests.question: If I were fluent in Mandarin,

quests.explanation: Second conditional uses 'were' (subjunctive) to signal an imaginary situation. The speaker isn't fluent (imaginary). If they were (unreal), they would move to Shanghai (would + infinitive). Note: 'were' is correct for all persons in formal English, not 'was'.
